description: A chief engineer suspects that a recurring equipment anomaly is real, but needs to compare log entries across several voyages to determine whether the same pattern has been appearing under similar conditions. All vessel and equipment names are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 48-year-old chief engineer with deep memory of the vessel but fragmented written logs
user_profile.context: The anomaly is subtle enough that each occurrence was previously dismissed in isolation
user_profile.communication_style: Forensic and skeptical, wants patterns proven from recorded details rather than intuition

fact_sheet.fact: The vessel in question is the MV 'Stellar Horizon', with IMO number 9876543.
The MV 'Stellar Horizon' is a Panamax bulk carrier operated by Orion Maritime Logistics.
The Chief Engineer investigating the anomaly is Alistair Finch.
Alistair Finch's employee ID with Orion Maritime Logistics is 77401.
The equipment experiencing anomalies is the primary Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO) Purifier, a 'Maritech Purifier Pro' model 8000.
The serial number of the HFO Purifier is MTPP-8K-915B2.
The normal operating back-pressure for the Maritech Purifier Pro 8000 is 2.5 bar.
All engine room logs are stored in a centralized database system named 'SeaLogix', version 4.2.
Alistair Finch accesses the SeaLogix system via the URL https://orion.sealogix.net using the username 'finch.a'.
The first voyage under review is V-SH-2208, from Singapore to Port Hedland, Australia, dated August 10-22, 2022.
On August 18, 2022, at 15:30 UTC (Voyage V-SH-2208), the HFO purifier back-pressure dropped to 2.1 bar for 11 minutes.
During the August 18, 2022 incident, the main engine load was at 88% and the sea water temperature was 30°C.
The log entry for the August 18, 2022 event (ID: 98A55) was annotated by the Second Engineer as 'Transient pressure dip, self-resolved'.
The second voyage under review is V-SH-2301, from Colombo, Sri Lanka to Fujairah, UAE, dated January 5-14, 2023.
On January 11, 2023, at 04:15 UTC (Voyage V-SH-2301), the HFO purifier back-pressure dropped to 2.0 bar for 14 minutes.
During the January 11, 2023 incident, the vessel was navigating the Arabian Sea with an ambient humidity of 89%.
The third voyage under review is V-SH-2305, from Santos, Brazil to Rotterdam, Netherlands, dated May 2-18, 2023.
On May 8, 2023, at 22:40 UTC (Voyage V-SH-2305), the HFO purifier back-pressure dropped to 2.1 bar for 9 minutes.
During the May 8, 2023 incident, the main engine was operating at 91% MCR (Maximum Continuous Rating) while crossing the equator.
The purifier's discharge pressure sensor (Model: Sensorex PT-100) was last calibrated on December 15, 2022.
A full service of the purifier bowl assembly was completed on December 16, 2022, at the Dubai Drydocks.
The SeaLogix system allows data export to CSV format for trend analysis in Microsoft Excel.
The Second Engineer on duty during the incident of January 11, 2023 was Jian Li.
Orion Maritime Logistics policy OML-ENG-113A requires a 'Root Cause Analysis Report' for any equipment anomaly recurring more than twice in a 12-month period.
The HFO being used during all three incidents was VLSFO (Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil) sourced from bunkering operations in Singapore.
The specific query Alistair Finch uses to find the anomalies is: `SELECT * FROM eng_log WHERE equipment_sn = 'MTPP-8K-915B2' AND parameter = 'back_pressure' AND value < 2.2`.
